g.text: get components ready to be stopped
component is ready to be stopped
A component is only ready to be stopped once every component
that depends on it has been stopped. So a transition stops
the components in the reverse of their start order.
deactivation is taken by a free worker
Supervision is stopped before the process is asked to
terminate, so the shutdown is not reported as a
wait for the process to exit
[the process exits within the shutdown timeout]
look up the component for the process id
look up the component for the process id
This may be the case for self-terminating processes.
In this case there is nothing further todo.
A deactivation has no failure outcome: the component
escalates until the process is gone.
next components ready to be stopped
Once everything that has to be stopped is gone, the
transition moves on to starting the components of the
target Run Target - see Component Activation.
[the graph has left the transition meanwhile]
The result is still consumed. Once the last component
in flight has reported back, the graph settles in
The two queues are the only interaction between the threads: the graph never
touches a component directly and a worker never touches the graph. All graph
and transition state stays confined to the main loop thread.
Several components may be in flight at the same time; a single one is shown
